body.title: LLD-0765b3a578e43eec-s2's --no-deps protection claim does not hold against the real pip-audit binary
body.reproduction: 1. Build a real wheel 'fakepkg' (setup.py install_requires=["privatelib"]), built with `pip wheel . --no-deps` so building it doesn't itself require resolving privatelib. 2. Write a requirements.txt containing only `fakepkg==1.0.0`. 3. Run `pip-audit -f json -r requirements.txt --no-deps` with PIP_FIND_LINKS pointing at the wheel's directory. Observed: pip-audit's own underlying `pip install --dry-run` step still attempts to resolve privatelib (fails if privatelib is unresolvable anywhere; if a second real wheel for privatelib is placed in the same PIP_FIND_LINKS directory, pip-audit's real JSON output then lists privatelib as an audited dependency entry too, with an identical result whether --no-deps is passed or omitted). Expected per the approved LLD (revision 6): '--no-deps' should make pip-audit treat the generated file as the complete, closed set, so privatelib (never named in requirements.txt) is never resolved or reported on at all. This was reproduced twice as collect-dependency-advisories.live.test.ts's own two scenarios.
body.rootCause: src/workflow/security-review/collect-dependency-advisories.ts:525-553 sets noDeps:true only for a pipenv/poetry requirementsPath generated by generateLockfileExport (src/workflow/security-review/lockfile-export.ts:201-232), and threads it through to pkgAuditTool's auditArgv in src/daemon/tools/builtins/pkg/index.ts:168-177,504,514, which appends the literal '--no-deps' flag to the pip-audit argv. This code is a correct implementation of the LLD's own instruction. The LLD's documented premise (docs/epics/add-dedicated-security-reviews-E202611100765b3a5/S002/LLD.md, revision 6, section on noDeps for excluded entries) is itself factually wrong: pip-audit's --no-deps flag does not disable the dependency-resolution step of its own underlying pip install --dry-run call. The real protection against a deliberately-excluded package reappearing is NOT this flag; it is that generateLockfileExport never writes the excluded package's name into the generated requirements.txt in the first place (confirmed: collectDependencyAdvisories's own mapPipAuditOutput, src/workflow/security-review/collect-dependency-advisories.ts:147-193, already quarantines any unexpectedly-returned name into unresolvedDependencies/unavailableSources rather than matches/queriedCoordinates, so no silent 'clean' or fabricated 'confirmed finding' results even in this scenario). This is documented directly in the live test's own comments, which independently recorded the same finding: src/workflow/security-review/__tests__/collect-dependency-advisories.live.test.ts:23-39,160-236.
body.fixIntent: Amend LLD-0765b3a578e43eec-s2 to remove or correct the claim that '--no-deps' itself prevents an excluded entry from being silently reintroduced via another exported package's transitive dependency, and instead document the actually-confirmed mechanism: the exclusion is enforced upstream, by generateLockfileExport never writing the excluded package's name into the generated requirements file, with collectDependencyAdvisories' own mapping quarantining any dependency pip-audit still returns outside that generated set. No code change to collectDependencyAdvisories, mapPipAuditOutput or generateLockfileExport is implied -- their current behavior is already safe and independently verified. This correction resolves Story s2 Task t6's one disputed build-gate acceptance check, which is worded against the LLD's current (incorrect) premise.
